title: The player who once stopped a war: Didier Drogba and Ivory Coast (2005–2007)
post:
8 October 2005: Ivory Coast reach their first World Cup, and in the dressing room Didier Drogba takes a microphone, kneels with his team-mates and begs both sides of a divided country to lay down their weapons. In 2007 the national team played in Bouaké, the rebels' capital, in front of soldiers from both sides.

#drogba #ivorycoast #cotedivoire #football #footballstory #footballhistory #worldcup #footballtiktok

voice._name: Callum (ElevenLabs premade), eleven_v3 with audio tags in "say"; a grave, warm read: short sentences, the name held back to the end of the opening

phrases.text: This player once stopped a war. Not with an army. With a microphone, on his knees, in a dressing room. His name? Didier Drogba.
phrases.say: [grave] This player once stopped a war. ... Not with an army. With a microphone... on his knees... in a dressing room. ... His name? ... Didier Drogba.

phrases.text: October 2005. Ivory Coast win in Sudan, their rivals Cameroon miss a last-minute penalty, and Ivory Coast reach their first World Cup.
phrases.say: October two thousand and five. Ivory Coast win in Sudan, their rivals Cameroon miss a last-minute penalty... [excited] and Ivory Coast reach their first World Cup!

phrases.text: The dressing room should be a party. Instead, in front of a national TV camera, Drogba takes the microphone.
phrases.say: The dressing room should be a party. ... [quietly] Instead, in front of a national TV camera, Drogba takes the microphone.

phrases.text: Because back home, his country has been cut in two for three years: rebels in the north, the army in the south. A civil war.
phrases.say: [grave] Because back home, his country has been cut in two, for three years: rebels in the north, the army in the south. ... A civil war.

phrases.text: So the whole team kneels. And he begs both sides: please, lay down your weapons.
phrases.say: [solemn] So the whole team kneels. And he begs both sides: ... please, lay down your weapons.

phrases.text: The clip plays on television for weeks. Both sides return to the table. In March 2007, they sign a peace deal.
phrases.say: The clip plays on television, for weeks. Both sides return to the table. In March two thousand and seven, they sign a peace deal.

phrases.text: Then Drogba asks for one more thing: play the next home match in Bouaké, the rebel capital. Soldiers from both sides watch the same game, in the same stadium. Ivory Coast win 5–0. Drogba scores the fifth.
phrases.say: Then Drogba asks for one more thing: play the next home match in Bwah-kay, the rebel capital. ... [building] Soldiers from both sides watch the same game, in the same stadium. Ivory Coast win five–nil. [awed] Drogba scores the fifth.

phrases.text: Next morning, one headline reads: five goals to erase five years of war.
phrases.say: [quietly] Next morning, one headline reads: ... five goals, to erase five years of war.
